title: Bitcoin Node
description: Chain sync, peers, mempool, fees and block statistics from bitcoin-prometheus-exporter.

panels.title: Node
panels.description: 1 when the exporter's liveness probe reached the node during the last scrape.

panels.title: Chain
panels.description: Network the node is validating.

panels.title: Version
panels.description: User agent the node advertises to its peers.

panels.title: Block height
panels.description: Height of the most-work fully validated chain.

panels.title: Peers
panels.description: Total peer connections, inbound and outbound.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: How long the node process has been running.

panels.title: Verified
panels.description: Share of chain work the node has verified. Below 1 means it is still catching up.

panels.title: Blocks behind headers
panels.description: Known headers minus validated blocks. Sustained non-zero means the node is not keeping up.

panels.title: Time since last block
panels.description: Age of the chain tip. Mainnet averages ten minutes; a steadily climbing line means no new blocks are arriving.

panels.title: Block store on disk
panels.description: Estimated size of the block and undo files.

panels.title: Peer connections
panels.description: Inbound peers find you; outbound peers you chose. A node with no outbound peers is trivially eclipsed.

panels.title: Peer round-trip time
panels.description: Aggregate ping across connected peers.

panels.title: Network traffic
panels.description: Peer-to-peer traffic rate in each direction.

panels.title: Peers by network
panels.description: Which transports the node's peers are reachable over.

panels.title: Peers by user agent
panels.description: Top eight peer implementations by count.

panels.title: Peers by connection type
panels.description: How each connection was established.

panels.title: Transactions in mempool
panels.description: Unconfirmed transactions the node is holding.

panels.title: Mempool memory
panels.description: Memory the mempool occupies against the configured ceiling. When usage reaches the ceiling the node evicts its cheapest transactions and raises its minimum relay fee.

panels.title: Minimum fee to enter the mempool
panels.description: The mempool minimum rises above the relay floor once the mempool is full.

panels.title: Fee estimates by confirmation target
panels.description: What the node thinks it costs to confirm within N blocks. Targets are ordered, so the shades run light to dark with patience. Empty on regtest and on a node with no fee history.

panels.title: Fee rates paid in the block at the tip
panels.description: Fee-rate distribution inside the most recent block: what miners actually accepted.

panels.title: Transactions per block
panels.description: Transaction count of the block at the tip.

panels.title: Block weight
panels.description: Weight of the block at the tip, against the 4,000,000 consensus limit.

panels.title: Fees and subsidy per block
panels.description: What the miner of the tip block earned, in satoshis.

panels.title: Collector success
panels.description: Per-collector outcome of each scrape. A collector can fail without taking the rest down.

panels.title: Collector scrape duration
panels.description: Time each collector spent talking to the node.

panels.title: RPC call rate
panels.description: JSON-RPC calls the exporter makes, and how many of them fail.

panels.title: RPC latency
panels.description: How long the node takes to answer.
